unit.title: Area and Perimeter
unit.blurb: Finding the perimeter of rectangles and shapes made of rectangles, and the area of rectangles by counting squares and by multiplying.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Measure and calculate the perimeter of rectangles and simple compound shapes.

O2.t: Find the area of rectangles and shapes made from rectangles, in square centimetres and square metres.

p: The **perimeter** is the total distance all the way round a shape. Add the lengths of all the sides.
For a rectangle: perimeter = length + width + length + width = **2 × (length + width)**.

lesson.t: Why we find missing sides first
p: For shapes with right angles, opposite sides that line up must add to the same total. Finding missing sides lets us add them all.

lesson.q: An L-shape has outside measurements 10 cm by 8 cm. Its perimeter?
steps: The steps in an L add up to the full length and width

lesson.t: Find the perimeter of a compound shape

p: A rectangle has 4 sides: don't just add the two lengths you can see labelled.

p: The **area** is the space inside a shape. We measure it in **square units**: square centimetres (**cm²**) or square metres (**m²**).
A rectangle 5 cm by 3 cm has 3 rows of 5 squares: **area = length × width = 15 cm²**.
A compound shape can be split into rectangles. Each rectangle's area is length × width; adding them gives the whole area.

lesson.q: An L-shape is made of a 6 cm × 4 cm rectangle and a 3 cm × 2 cm rectangle. Find its area.

lesson.t: Find the area of a compound shape

p: Area counts the squares inside (cm²); perimeter measures the distance round (cm).
